tagline: Sync sprint data from Jira into Airtable for cross-functional reporting
metaTitle: Jira + Airtable Integration: Jira Issues as Airtable Records
metaDescription: Sync Jira issues to Airtable records and send Airtable intake forms to the Jira backlog. GAIA builds roadmap views. See the setup steps.
intro:
Operations, program management, and business teams love Airtable for its flexible views, formulas, and reporting. Engineering teams depend on Jira for sprint management, issue tracking, and release planning. When these groups need to collaborate on roadmaps, resourcing, or executive reporting, the data gap between the two forces manual exports and stale spreadsheets.

GAIA bridges that gap in real time. Issues, epics, sprints, and version data flow into Airtable records automatically, giving business teams the database views they need without a Jira license. Intake forms generate tickets automatically. Executive dashboards built on those records pull live sprint velocity and burn-down data.

For enterprise organizations that run a cross-functional operations hub in Airtable, this integration makes engineering delivery data a first-class citizen in every operational report.

useCases.title: Jira issues as Airtable records
useCases.description: GAIA syncs issues to a configured table, with a record for each ticket containing status, assignee, priority, sprint, fix version, and story points, updated in real time.

useCases.title: Airtable intake forms to Jira backlog
useCases.description: Business teams submit requests via forms. GAIA converts qualifying submissions into backlog issues automatically and writes the ticket link back to the originating record.

useCases.title: Executive roadmap dashboard
useCases.description: GAIA feeds epic and version data into a dedicated base configured as an executive roadmap view, giving leadership accurate delivery timelines without access to the issue tracker.

useCases.title: Sprint velocity tracking
useCases.description: GAIA writes sprint velocity and story point completion data to the table after each sprint, enabling operations teams to build capacity planning models using native formulas.

useCases.title: SLA monitoring for customer-linked tickets
useCases.description: GAIA syncs tickets tagged with customer identifiers into the base and triggers alerts when they approach or breach SLA thresholds, based on automation rules in the base.

howItWorks.description: Authenticate both accounts in GAIA's settings. Specify the base and table where issue data should be synced.

howItWorks.step: Map Jira fields to Airtable columns
howItWorks.description: Define the mapping between issue fields and table columns. GAIA provides a default schema covering standard fields and supports custom field mapping for advanced configurations.

howItWorks.step: GAIA keeps records current with live data
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors for changes and updates records in real time. Form submissions are also monitored and converted to issues on a configurable schedule.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync Jira epics and sprints as well as individual issues?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can sync epics, sprints, and versions to separate tables or as linked records, giving you a relational database view of your entire project structure.

faqs.question: Can Airtable users update tickets by editing records?
faqs.answer: Selective writeback is supported. You can configure specific columns (like assignee or priority) to push updates back to the ticket when changed in the record, while keeping other fields read-only.

faqs.question: How often does GAIA sync data between the two?
faqs.answer: By default, GAIA syncs in near real time for high-signal events (status changes, assignments, new issues) and on a periodic schedule for bulk data like sprint velocity metrics.

faqs.question: Can I use this to build a public-facing roadmap?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can sync a filtered subset of issues (e.g., issues tagged as public roadmap items) to a base configured for public sharing, giving you a live roadmap without manual updates.
